prompt: The first ARPANET message was sent between UCLA and Stanford
explanation: The first host-to-host message on ARPANET was sent from UCLA to the Stanford Research Institute, a foundational moment in networked computing.

prompt: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email using the @ symbol
explanation: Ray Tomlinson adapted email for networked computers and chose @ to separate the user name from the host machine.

prompt: Ethernet was invented at Xerox PARC
explanation: Bob Metcalfe and colleagues developed Ethernet as a way to connect computers on local networks.

prompt: Microsoft was founded
explanation: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft as the personal-computer software industry began to take shape.

prompt: MTV launched and helped define a new era of music video culture
explanation: MTV launched as a cable channel built around music videos and became deeply influential in youth and pop culture.

prompt: Apple launched the original Macintosh
explanation: The Macintosh brought a graphical user interface and mouse-driven interaction to a mass consumer audience.

prompt: Microsoft released Windows 1.0
explanation: Windows 1.0 introduced a graphical shell for MS-DOS and began a software line that would dominate desktop computing.

prompt: Nintendo released the Game Boy
explanation: The Game Boy made portable cartridge gaming mainstream and became one of Nintendo’s defining hardware products.

prompt: The first web server and browser were built at CERN
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee built the first web server and browser-editor on a NeXT computer at CERN.

prompt: Linus Torvalds announced the Linux kernel project
explanation: Torvalds announced a free Unix-like operating-system kernel that became central to servers, cloud infrastructure and Android.

prompt: CERN placed the World Wide Web software into the public domain
explanation: CERN made the web technology freely available, helping accelerate adoption worldwide.

prompt: Netscape was founded and began building a commercial web browser
explanation: Netscape helped turn the web browser into a mass-market gateway to the Internet during the first browser boom.

prompt: The first widely cited web banner ad appeared on HotWired
explanation: AT&T’s clickable HotWired banner is widely remembered as the first major web banner advertisement.

prompt: eBay launched as AuctionWeb
explanation: Pierre Omidyar launched AuctionWeb, which grew into eBay and helped normalize person-to-person commerce online.

prompt: Java was publicly released by Sun Microsystems
explanation: Java promoted the idea of portable software that could run across different computer systems.

prompt: ICQ launched and popularized instant messaging
explanation: ICQ helped make real-time presence and instant messaging a normal part of being online.

prompt: Google.com was registered as a domain name
explanation: The google.com domain was registered before Google formally incorporated the following year.

prompt: SixDegrees launched as an early profile-and-friends social network
explanation: SixDegrees combined personal profiles and friend lists years before social networking became mainstream.

prompt: The company that became PayPal was founded
explanation: Confinity was founded in 1998 and later evolved into PayPal, a major force in online payments.

prompt: Blogger launched and helped popularize personal publishing on the web
explanation: Blogger lowered the barrier to publishing regularly online and became one of the services associated with the rise of blogging.

prompt: Salesforce launched with a cloud-first software model
explanation: Salesforce helped popularize software delivered over the Internet instead of installed on customer servers.

prompt: Sony released the PlayStation 2
explanation: The PlayStation 2 became the best-selling home video-game console and also helped normalize DVD playback in living rooms.

prompt: Apple introduced the iPod
explanation: The iPod made large digital music libraries portable and became a major part of Apple’s consumer comeback.

prompt: The Tor project released its first public software
explanation: Tor grew from onion-routing research into a widely used system for privacy-preserving Internet communication.

prompt: Skype launched
explanation: Skype made Internet voice calling accessible to a mass audience and became synonymous with online calling.

prompt: Valve launched Steam
explanation: Steam began as a software distribution and update platform and grew into the dominant PC game storefront.

prompt: Google launched Gmail
explanation: Gmail launched with unusually large storage and conversation-style email threads, reshaping expectations for webmail.

prompt: Mozilla Firefox 1.0 was released
explanation: Firefox became a major open-source browser challenger during the post-Netscape browser era.

prompt: Reddit launched
explanation: Reddit grew from a link-sharing site into one of the Internet’s largest networks of topic-based communities.

prompt: Google Maps launched
explanation: Google Maps brought interactive online maps and later turn-by-turn navigation to a huge global audience.

prompt: Amazon Web Services launched S3
explanation: Amazon S3 became one of the foundational services of modern cloud computing.

prompt: Spotify was founded
explanation: Spotify was founded in Sweden before launching its streaming service commercially in 2008.

prompt: Amazon released the first Kindle
explanation: The Kindle connected an e-reader directly to an online bookstore and helped mainstream digital books.

prompt: Tumblr launched
explanation: Tumblr mixed blogging, fandom and social following into a distinctive Internet culture platform.

prompt: Google Chrome launched
explanation: Chrome entered a competitive browser market and later became the world’s most widely used web browser.

prompt: Apple opened the iPhone App Store
explanation: The App Store created a centralized marketplace for mobile software and helped ignite the modern app economy.

prompt: The Bitcoin network produced its genesis block
explanation: Bitcoin’s first block marked the operational beginning of the decentralized cryptocurrency network.

prompt: The first public version of Minecraft was released
explanation: Minecraft began as an indie sandbox project and grew into one of the best-selling games ever made.

prompt: Apple released the first iPad
explanation: The iPad helped create a mainstream market for modern touchscreen tablets.

prompt: Pinterest launched
explanation: Pinterest built a visual bookmarking network around collections, inspiration and discovery.

prompt: Twitch launched as a live-streaming platform focused on gaming
explanation: Twitch turned live game streaming into a mainstream creator and spectator format.

prompt: Apple introduced Siri on the iPhone 4S
explanation: Siri brought a conversational voice assistant to a mass-market smartphone audience.

prompt: Oculus Rift became a breakout Kickstarter project
explanation: The Oculus Rift crowdfunding campaign reignited mainstream interest in consumer virtual reality.

prompt: Google Drive launched
explanation: Google Drive combined cloud file storage with Google’s collaborative productivity tools.

prompt: Edward Snowden’s disclosures triggered a global debate over Internet surveillance
explanation: The disclosures revealed large-scale government surveillance programs and changed public discussion about privacy and encryption.

prompt: Slack launched its workplace messaging product
explanation: Slack helped move workplace communication from email toward persistent channels and integrations.

prompt: Amazon introduced the Echo smart speaker and Alexa
explanation: Echo brought always-available voice assistants into the home and helped popularize smart speakers.

prompt: Amazon acquired Twitch
explanation: Amazon bought Twitch as live-streaming audiences and gaming culture were rapidly expanding.

prompt: Apple Watch went on sale
explanation: Apple’s smartwatch became a major new wearable-computing product category for the company.

prompt: OpenAI was founded
explanation: OpenAI was founded as an artificial-intelligence research organization years before ChatGPT brought it mass attention.

prompt: AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol
explanation: DeepMind’s AlphaGo defeated one of the world’s strongest Go players, a landmark moment for machine learning.

prompt: Facebook opened Messenger to chatbots
explanation: Messenger’s bot platform kicked off a major wave of interest in conversational interfaces before modern generative AI.

prompt: The WannaCry ransomware attack spread around the world
explanation: WannaCry disrupted hospitals, companies and public agencies across many countries by exploiting vulnerable Windows systems.

prompt: ByteDance launched TikTok internationally
explanation: TikTok launched outside China before later merging with Musical.ly and accelerating its global growth.

prompt: The European Union’s GDPR took effect
explanation: GDPR reshaped how companies around the world handled personal data, consent and privacy rights.

prompt: Fortnite arrived on mobile devices
explanation: Fortnite’s mobile release extended the battle-royale phenomenon across phones, consoles and PCs.

prompt: Google launched Stadia cloud gaming
explanation: Stadia attempted to make high-end games streamable without a traditional console, though the service was later shut down.

prompt: Apple released AirPods Pro
explanation: AirPods Pro added active noise cancellation and helped cement wireless earbuds as a mainstream everyday device.

prompt: Zoom became a defining tool of remote work and school during the pandemic
explanation: Zoom usage exploded as offices, schools and families moved daily activity online during COVID-19 lockdowns.

prompt: Animal Crossing: New Horizons became a lockdown-era social phenomenon
explanation: Nintendo’s island life game became a major online social space during the early months of the pandemic.

prompt: Facebook changed its corporate name to Meta
explanation: The company rebranded around its metaverse ambitions while Facebook remained the name of its flagship social network.

prompt: Beeple’s digital artwork sold at Christie’s for $69 million
explanation: The high-profile NFT sale became one of the defining moments of the 2021 crypto-art boom.

prompt: OpenAI introduced DALL·E 2
explanation: DALL·E 2 helped bring high-quality text-to-image generation into mainstream technology discussion.

prompt: Elon Musk completed his acquisition of Twitter
explanation: Musk’s acquisition led to sweeping product, staffing and policy changes before Twitter was later renamed X.

prompt: OpenAI released GPT-4
explanation: GPT-4 marked a major capability jump in OpenAI’s general-purpose language models and introduced image understanding in the model family.

prompt: Apple unveiled Vision Pro
explanation: Apple introduced Vision Pro as a spatial-computing headset before shipping it to customers in 2024.

prompt: OpenAI previewed Sora, a text-to-video model
explanation: Sora demonstrated long-form text-to-video generation and became one of the year’s most discussed generative-AI demos.

prompt: A faulty CrowdStrike update caused a massive global Windows outage
explanation: A defective security update crashed Windows systems across airlines, banks, hospitals and other organizations worldwide.

prompt: DeepSeek released the R1 reasoning model
explanation: DeepSeek R1 drew global attention for strong reasoning performance and intensified competition around efficient AI models.

prompt: Nintendo released the Switch 2
explanation: Nintendo launched the successor to the original Switch after years of anticipation around its next-generation console.
